name: Beriah Palmer
bio: A Representative from New York; born in Bristol County, Mass., in 1740; attended the common schools; moved to Cornwall, Orange County, N.Y., in 1769; studied law; was admitted to the bar and practiced in New York; engaged in surveying and farming near Burnt Hills; moved to Ballston Spa, Saratoga County, N.Y., in 1774; served in the Revolutionary War, Twelfth Regiment of the New York Militia; served as assessor in 1779; commissioner of roads, district of Ballston, 1780, 1783, and 1784; served as postmaster in 1784; member of the committee of safety of Albany County, N.Y.; supervisor of Saratoga County, N.Y., 1790, 1791, and 1799; moderator of the first board of supervisors of Saratoga County. N.Y., 1791; appointed judge of the court of common pleas in 1791; member of the New York assembly, 1792-1795; delegate to the New York state constitutional convention, 1801; elected as a Democratic Republican to the Eighth Congress (March 4, 1803-March 3, 1805); surrogate of Saratoga County, N.Y., 1808-1812; died on May 20, 1812, in Ballston Spa, N.Y.; interment in the Village Cemetery, Ballston Spa, N.Y.
